correctness.rationale: In the square-grid cover each deck map has normal form h^p v^q; for q nonzero its vertical displacement is |q|L, and otherwise a nonidentity map has horizontal displacement at least L. Hence walks shorter than L close upstairs if closed downstairs. There are no triangles, and simple four-cycles are exactly projected unit squares since L≥5; projections of squares are embedded and distinct. The group before filling is free of rank E−V+1=L²+1. The square-filled complexes are the torus and Klein bottle, with the stated presentations. Other disks before L attach along nullhomotopic loops and give isomorphisms on π1. A row and the x=0 column are simple length-L representatives of the deck generators, so the quotient group is trivial at L and thereafter. Over F₂ the square boundary matrix has its one face relation: an edge forces its two incident faces to have equal coefficients in the kernel, and the dual graph is connected. The dimensions are thus L²+1, two and zero; the natural maps are surjective, so there are no later births and the full barcodes agree. Integral homology would distinguish the middle groups, consistently with the stated mod-two scope.
residual_risks: The independent replay verifies binary cycle ranks in two cases, not their unrestricted values or the nonabelian groups. Those follow from the covering and cellular arguments.
